ideas.title: Tactile Suit-Rank Corner Clips
ideas.concept: A boxed set of 52 small clip-on tabs, each shaped for one suit (via a distinct outer notch silhouette) and rank (via a raised braille-style pip cluster on the top face), that snap friction-fit over the corner of any standard bridge/poker-size playing card so a low-vision or blind player can identify the card by touch alone.
ideas.rationale: Documented, verifiable accessibility gap: BGG/NFB/Future Insight articles on making board games accessible describe retrofitting existing decks with tactile/braille labels as a manual craft workaround (glue, puffy paint, Velcro), and commercial solutions (thelowvisionstore.com, Independent Living Aids) only sell pre-printed dedicated braille decks for specific classic games rather than a retrofit for a player's own game collection.
ideas.differentiation: Search for 3D-printed accessible card solutions turned up dedicated braille playing-card decks (fixed, single-purpose, must be purchased whole) and separate non-tactile card-holding clips (Printables 'Card Clip' by OderWat, for stability only, no tactile code). No result combined a detachable, per-corner tactile suit+rank clip that retrofits a player's own existing deck of any game. Claim is scoped narrowly to that specific retrofit-clip mechanism, not to accessible gaming in general.
ideas.producibility_notes: 52 small parts per full-deck kit (13 ranks x 4 suit-notch shapes), single color PLA, no assembly, print-in-place not needed (each clip is a solid single-piece slide-on tab). One critical tolerance: the card+sleeve slot gap, target 0.9mm nominal clearance (card ~0.3mm + standard single sleeve ~0.6mm) with a customer-selectable +0.2mm option for double-sleeved cards.
ideas.margin_case: Roughly 20g PLA total for a 52-clip set, ~2hr print on a single plate. Sell at $29 for a full-deck kit vs. $15-25 commercial braille decks that only work for one specific game each; buyer pays once to make their entire existing card-game collection accessible.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a set of 52 small plastic clips, one per playing card in a standard 52-card deck, that slide onto the corner of a card to add tactile identification. Each clip has a U-shaped slot on its underside sized to grip over one corner of a standard bridge/poker card (with or without a protective sleeve). The top face of each clip has a raised braille-style cluster of 1-4 small hemispherical bumps (2mm diameter, 1mm height) arranged in a fixed 2x2 grid pattern encoding the card's rank 1-13. The outer edge silhouette of the clip is one of 4 distinct shapes (a rounded heart notch, a pointed spade notch, a diamond notch, a trefoil/club notch) encoding the suit, so the shape can also be felt by touch. Purpose: This is an accessibility retrofit kit for blind or low-vision tabletop/card-game hobbyists, letting them add tactile identification to any deck of cards they already own (not limited to one specific game) so they can play alongside sighted friends. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, smooth rounded edges safe for repeated finger contact, no sharp corners, single flat color per full set (customer may request a specific PLA color). Technical specification: Each clip is approximately 18mm x 14mm x 3mm. The card-gripping slot is a U-channel 0.9mm wide by 12mm deep by 10mm tall, with wall thickness of 1.2mm around the slot for durability; provide a customer-configurable slot-width parameter (0.7mm to 1.3mm) to accommodate unsleeved cards, single-sleeved, or double-sleeved decks. All 52 clips are single-color PLA, no assembly and no support material required if oriented with the slot opening facing up. Deliver as a full 52-piece set nested for efficient plate packing, with each clip individually labeled in the model filename by suit and rank.

ideas.title: Custom Engraved Player Nameplate Meeples
ideas.concept: A set of 4 to 6 oversized meeple-shaped stands, each approximately 45mm tall, with the buyer's chosen name or initials engraved into a plinth base plus a small choice of icon accent (star, crown, dice, paw print), used as personalized player markers for any board game or as party/wedding favors.
ideas.rationale: Etsy market pages for 'Custom Board Game Pieces' and 'Personalized Game' show sustained demand for name-customized tabletop pieces as gifts, and reviewers on those listings specifically cite requesting custom names/colors for family game-night sets, but current listings are either hand-finished one-off Etsy items with limited font/layout choice or static unpersonalized STL files that the buyer must customize and print themselves.
ideas.differentiation: Search shows free meeple STLs on Thingiverse/Printables are generic unpersonalized shapes, and Etsy custom meeples are individually hand-made with fixed style options per shop. This product's differentiation is structural, not geometric: a per-order parametric engraving pipeline (name text + icon selection generated fresh at order time) that a static file repository cannot offer, sold as a ready-made finished object rather than a DIY file.
ideas.producibility_notes: One part per meeple, single color PLA, no assembly, no multi-material. Critical dimension: debossed name text minimum stroke width 1mm and minimum depth 0.6mm to stay legible at 0.4mm nozzle resolution; base plinth diameter fixed at 22mm to keep text length constrained (auto-scale font down for longer names, cap at 10 characters).
ideas.margin_case: About 40g PLA for a 6-meeple set, ~1.5hr print. Sell at $24 for a set of 6 personalized meeples; buyer is paying for the personalization and finished convenience, not the plastic, comparable to $8-15 per-piece pricing seen on Etsy custom meeple listings for a fraction of the labor cost.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a single meeple-style figure (the classic rounded-head, flared-body pawn shape used in board games) mounted on a small cylindrical plinth base. The front face of the plinth base has a customer-supplied name or initials (up to 10 characters) debossed (recessed) into the surface in a clean sans-serif font, and the meeple's chest/body area has one small debossed icon selected from a fixed set of 4 options (a 5-point star, a crown, a six-sided die face, or a paw print). Purpose: This is a personalized player-identifier piece for board game night, sold as a set of 4-6, used as a gift for board-game enthusiasts, wedding/party favor, or family game-night table markers. Style: Clean, slightly stylized modern meeple silhouette (smooth rounded head, gently tapered flared skirt base, no fine ornamentation), single solid color per meeple (customer chooses one color for the whole set or a different color per meeple). Technical specification: Overall meeple height 45mm, plinth base diameter 22mm, plinth height 6mm. Single-part print, single color, no supports needed when printed standing upright on the flat base. Debossed text: minimum stroke width 1mm, recess depth 0.6mm, font size auto-scaled to fit the character count within the 22mm base diameter with 2mm margin. Icon deboss: 8mm diameter footprint, 0.5mm recess depth. No assembly, no hardware, no glue required. Generate one STL per meeple in the requested set size (4, 5, or 6 count) with the specified name and icon baked into each model.

ideas.title: Flip-and-Write Field Clipboard
ideas.concept: A rigid lap clipboard sized for standard flip-and-write score sheets, with a slide-out marker garage on one edge that holds a dry-erase marker and a felt eraser strip, a spring-clip sheet-retention lip at the top, and a single fold-out kickstand leg on the back so it can stand upright on a table.
ideas.rationale: Named genre trend: flip-and-write / roll-and-write games (Welcome To..., Cartographers, Silver & Gold, Second Chance) have been a consistently active BGG category for several years, and many of these titles are explicitly designed to be replayed indefinitely using printed or dry-erase community score sheets rather than the box's limited paper pad, creating recurring demand for a stable dry-erase writing surface.
ideas.differentiation: Search found standalone dry-erase marker clip holders (Printables, generic) and standalone flip/dry-erase scoreboards sold for a single specific game (Etsy 'Twice as Clever' acrylic sheet), but no result combined a lap clipboard, an integrated marker+eraser garage, and a fold-out table kickstand in one genre-agnostic part built for flip-and-write play generally. Claim is scoped to that specific 3-feature combination, not to dry-erase boards as a category.
ideas.producibility_notes: 2 parts (clipboard body, single kickstand leg on a printed living hinge), single color PLA, one living hinge (N=1, low risk per the single-flex-joint rule). Critical dimension: marker garage bore diameter 12mm with 0.3mm print clearance to snugly hold a standard fine-tip dry-erase marker barrel.
ideas.margin_case: Approximately 120g PLA, ~3.5hr print. Sell at $19; cheaper than assembling a separate clipboard, marker holder, and stand, and priced for the recurring roll-and-write player base who print community fan scoresheets and need a stable non-table writing surface.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a rigid rectangular clipboard sized to hold a standard A5/half-letter flip-and-write score sheet, with a top spring-style retention lip that pinches the sheet in place, a marker garage tube molded into the right-hand long edge sized to hold one standard fine-tip dry-erase marker with a felt eraser pad recessed into the garage's end cap, and a single fold-out kickstand leg attached via a printed living hinge on the back face that flips out to prop the board upright at a 60-degree angle on a table. Purpose: A portable writing surface for players of flip-and-write / roll-and-write board games (games where each player fills in their own printed score sheet each round), used at home game nights or gaming cafes, letting a player write comfortably without a hard table surface and always have their marker and eraser attached. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, flat matte finish, single solid color, no decorative ornamentation, subtle rounded corners for comfortable handling. Technical specification: Overall clipboard dimensions 170mm x 230mm x 4mm (body), marker garage tube 12mm inner diameter x 140mm long integrated along one edge, retention lip at the top is a 3mm-tall printed spring clip requiring no metal hardware. Kickstand leg: 80mm long, 15mm wide, attached via one 0.4mm-thick living hinge section, with a friction-fit stop tab that holds it open at 60 degrees. Single color PLA, two total printed parts fused via the living hinge (printed as one piece), no glue or screws, print flat with the kickstand leg laid open to avoid support material.

ideas.title: Modular Cycle Turn-Order Wheel
ideas.concept: A rotating disc turn-order tracker built from a central hub with a fixed pointer arm and 2 to 6 identical snap-in wedge segments (one per player) around the rim, so the same hub can be reconfigured for different player counts by adding or removing wedges rather than being manufactured fixed at one size.
ideas.rationale: Named, verifiable trend: Rebirth by Reiner Knizia won the 2026 Kennerspiel des Jahres (confirmed via ICv2 and wericmartin.com coverage of the July 2026 award announcement), and its core mechanic revolves around cyclical soul/rebirth progression, putting cyclical/repeating-turn game mechanics in front of a large enthusiast audience this year and creating a natural thematic hook for a cyclical turn-tracking accessory usable across any game with rotating turn order.
ideas.differentiation: Search for turn-order trackers found only fixed-slot designs (Printables 'Boardgame Turn Order Indicator', a flip-direction disc; Etsy 'Board Game Turn Tracker' laser-cut items) each built for one fixed player count. No result offered a snap-together wedge system letting the buyer add or remove player segments on the same hub. Claim is scoped to that specific modular-count mechanism, not to turn trackers broadly.
ideas.producibility_notes: 3 distinct part types: 1 hub+pointer, up to 6 identical wedge segments (buyer typically orders 4), single color PLA. One critical tolerance: wedge-to-hub dovetail snap interference fit at 0.15mm, sized for a firm push-fit that stays assembled during table use but can be pried off by hand to reconfigure.
ideas.margin_case: About 35g PLA for a hub plus 6 wedges, ~1.2hr print. Sell at $16 as a small impulse add-on alongside board game gifts; priced below the $20+ laser-cut wooden trackers on Etsy while offering reconfigurable player counts they don't.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a rotating turn-order tracker consisting of one central hub disc with a fixed radial pointer arm on top, and a set of 6 identical trapezoidal wedge segments that snap into a dovetail groove around the hub's circumference, so a player can assemble 2 to 6 wedges to match their game's player count and rotate the hub to point at the active wedge each turn. Purpose: A physical turn-order indicator used at the table in any multiplayer board game to show whose turn is next, sold as a generic accessory that works across a player's whole game collection regardless of player count. Style: Minimal/utilitarian geometric design with a subtle circular groove pattern suggesting a cyclical wheel motif, single solid color (customer-selectable), no game-specific branding or text. Technical specification: Hub disc 60mm diameter x 8mm thick with a central low-friction pivot boss (10mm diameter) so it spins freely when set on a table or a printed base ring; pointer arm extends 35mm from hub edge. Each wedge segment is 20mm x 25mm x 8mm with a dovetail tab on its inner edge sized 8mm wide x 4mm deep with a 0.15mm interference fit against the matching hub groove for a firm snap that can still be removed by hand. Provide the full set as: 1 hub+pointer part and 6 identical wedge parts, single color PLA, no glue, no hardware, no supports required if printed flat with the pivot boss facing up.

ideas.title: Gridfinity Sleeved-Card Vault
ideas.concept: A 2x2-module Gridfinity-baseplate-compatible storage bin that holds a stack of sleeved cards standing upright, using a spring-loaded follower block (one small compression spring) that keeps the deck pressed against a clear index window so cards can be flipped through and pulled out like a card catalog drawer.
ideas.rationale: Named, verifiable trend: Gridfinity is a widely adopted open modular storage standard within the 3D-printing hobby community (evidenced by dedicated generator tools, a public GitHub design catalog, and hundreds of Printables/MakerWorld listings), and board-gamers have visibly adopted it for token and component storage, per MakerWorld's 'Gridfinity Tabletop Board-game & Card-game Trays' listing and multiple community bin designs.
ideas.differentiation: Search for existing Gridfinity board-game card storage found open trading-card trays and flat bins (e.g. Bmorr's 'Gridfinity Trading Card Organizer' for MTG/Pokemon, MakerWorld's generic tabletop trays) that hold cards loose or stacked without retention. No result used a spring-loaded follower to keep an upright sleeved deck compressed and browsable. Claim is scoped to that specific spring-follower-plus-Gridfinity-footprint combination.
ideas.producibility_notes: 3 parts: bin shell (with Gridfinity-spec base geometry), follower block, end cap; single color PLA; one hardware insert (a single 20mm x 8mm off-the-shelf compression spring, justified because a printed cantilever spring would fatigue under repeated compression cycles while a $0.10 steel spring does not). Critical dimension: internal cavity width sized to sleeved-card width plus 1mm clearance (default target 67.5mm for a 66.5mm sleeved card, offered as a configurable parameter for other sleeve brands).
ideas.margin_case: About 90g PLA plus one spring, ~4hr print. Sell at $24; Gridfinity adopters have already invested in baseplates and consistently pay premium prices ($15-25 per specialty bin on Etsy 'Gridfinity Storage') for modules with exact-fit functionality their generic bins lack.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a rectangular storage bin conforming to the open-source Gridfinity modular storage standard (42mm x 42mm per grid unit, standard Gridfinity base profile with stacking lip and magnet/screw holes) sized as a 2x2 module footprint (84mm x 84mm x 60mm tall). Inside the bin, cards stand upright in a card-catalog orientation, pressed from the back by a sliding follower block that a compression spring pushes forward against the stack, with the front face of the bin open as an index window so the front card's top edge is visible and can be pulled straight up and out. Purpose: A card storage module for tabletop board-game and card-game hobbyists who use the Gridfinity system to organize sleeved playing cards or game cards densely and keep them browsable without removing the whole stack. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, matches the plain flat-wall aesthetic of standard Gridfinity bins, single solid color, no ornamentation. Technical specification: Overall footprint conforms exactly to 2x2 Gridfinity grid units (84mm x 84mm) at 60mm height, with the standard Gridfinity base lip and 4 corner magnet holes (6mm diameter x 2mm deep) for baseplate compatibility. Internal card cavity width 67.5mm (configurable), depth accommodates up to 60 sleeved standard-size cards (approximately 45mm stack depth) plus the follower block. Follower block: a flat plastic slider 65mm x 55mm x 8mm riding in internal rails with 0.3mm clearance, pushed by one 20mm-long x 8mm-diameter steel compression spring seated in a printed pocket at the rear wall. 3 total printed parts (bin shell, follower block, rear end cap that retains the spring), single color PLA, one spring hardware insert, no glue required, snap-fit rear cap with a 0.2mm interference fit.

ideas.title: Grip-Assist Piece Topper Retrofit Set
ideas.concept: A 15-piece kit of three snap-on topper types (5 dice toppers, 5 cardboard-standee base clips, 5 small-token pinch tabs) that fit over a player's existing dice, cardboard standees, and small tokens to add a large ribbed grip surface, letting players with arthritis or limited fine motor control keep using their own game collection instead of buying a whole replacement accessible edition.
ideas.rationale: Documented, verifiable demand: a free 'Easier to Handle Generic Game Tokens' model already exists on Printables specifically because, per its own listing description, some players 'have problems handling regular game tokens,' and commercial low-vision/limited-dexterity aids for card and board games (Rehabmart, LS&S Products, Independent Living Aids 'Games | Tactile' category) are an established retail category, confirming a real, ongoing buyer base for grip-accessible gaming products.
ideas.differentiation: The existing free Printables model replaces game tokens outright with new oversized pieces, and commercial dexterity aids in this niche are mostly card holders. Search found no retrofit topper that snaps over components the player already owns (their own dice, their own game's cardboard standees, their own tokens) without replacing them. Claim is scoped narrowly to that specific non-destructive retrofit approach, not to accessible gaming tokens broadly.
ideas.producibility_notes: 15 parts total across 3 shape families (5 identical dice toppers, 5 identical standee clips, 5 identical token pinch-tabs), single color PLA with 0.6mm-tall printed knurl ribs for grip texture (kept single-material rather than TPU to avoid multi-material complexity). Critical dimension: dice-topper inner socket sized for a standard 16mm six-sided die with 0.3mm clearance for a firm snap-fit that still allows removal.
ideas.margin_case: About 50g PLA for the full 15-piece kit, ~2hr print. Sell at $21; positioned against $15-20 commercial dexterity aids that each cover only one component type (e.g. card holders alone), while this kit covers three common component types a player already owns.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a 15-piece kit of three distinct snap-on grip toppers. Type A (qty 5): a hollow dome cap with an internal socket sized to snap over a standard 16mm six-sided die, with raised 0.6mm-tall ribbed knurling on the dome's outer surface for grip. Type B (qty 5): a U-shaped clip that slides over the bottom edge of a flat cardboard standee/tile (typically 2mm thick) and extends upward into a wider knurled tab that stands proud above the standee so it can be pinched and moved without touching the thin cardboard. Type C (qty 5): a wraparound pinch-tab that snaps around a small wooden or plastic cube/token (8-16mm, adjustable) leaving two opposing knurled finger-pad wings protruding on either side for an easy pinch grip. Purpose: An accessibility retrofit kit for board-game players with arthritis, tremor, or limited fine motor control, letting them add large grip surfaces to dice, standees, and tokens they already own rather than replacing their existing game collection. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, smooth rounded edges everywhere except the functional ribbed grip zones, single solid color (customer-selectable, high-contrast colors like orange or yellow recommended for low-vision users too). Technical specification: Type A dome topper outer diameter 24mm, inner die socket 16.3mm (0.3mm clearance snap-fit over a 16mm die), knurl ribs 0.6mm tall spaced 2mm apart. Type B clip channel 2.2mm wide x 15mm deep to grip a 2mm-thick standee, tab rises 20mm above the standee top edge, tab width 18mm with knurling. Type C wraparound tab has an adjustable-width parameter (8mm to 16mm) for the token being gripped, with two 15mm x 10mm knurled finger wings. All 15 parts single-color PLA, no assembly, no glue, no supports needed if each part is oriented with its largest flat face down.

ideas.title: Legacy Campaign Spoiler Vault
ideas.concept: A lidded storage box sized to hold a stack of sealed legacy-game envelopes or mini-boxes (the kind found in Gloomhaven, Frosthaven, Pandemic Legacy, and similar campaign games), with the lid held shut by a single embedded magnetic catch that only releases when a separate printed 'key' disc (also magnet-embedded) is pressed against a marked spot on the lid, plus an internal slot that holds a printed session-tracker card noting which campaign milestone unlocks the vault.
ideas.rationale: Documented community behavior: BGG threads and the Gloomhaven Wiki describe sealed legacy envelopes/boxes as being opened 'as a ceremony,' with accidentally seeing them considered a serious etiquette breach, and BGG search results note an active hobbyist 3D-printing community around legacy-game storage where 'taming the box is half the hobby' — establishing both the ceremonial framing and an existing willingness to buy printed accessories for these specific games.
ideas.differentiation: Search for legacy-game 3D print accessories found only generic component organizers/inserts (storage only, no locking mechanism) and, separately, generic printable combination/puzzle lock boxes with no board-game framing. No result combined a magnetic single-catch lock, an envelope-sized compartment, and a session-tracker card slot purpose-built for legacy-game campaign content. Claim is scoped to that specific compound, not to lock boxes or organizers generally.
ideas.producibility_notes: 3 parts (box, lid, key disc), single color PLA, 2 small neodymium magnets as a hardware insert (justified: a single magnetic catch is a low mechanical risk mechanism compared to a multi-wafer combination lock, and magnets cost about $0.20 each). Critical dimension: internal compartment sized 90mm x 130mm x 40mm deep to fit stacked standard legacy-game envelopes and small boxes.
ideas.margin_case: About 140g PLA plus 2 magnets, ~5hr print. Sell at $27; legacy-campaign groups have already demonstrated willingness to pay $80-100+ for official legacy games with destructible/sealed content, making a modest-premium ceremonial storage accessory a plausible add-on purchase for the same audience.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a two-part lidded box with a magnetic locking mechanism. The box body has an internal compartment for storing stacked sealed envelopes or small boxes, plus a narrow side slot that holds a single printed index card face-out. The lid closes flush over the body and is held shut by one 8mm neodymium disc magnet embedded in the lid aligned with a matching magnet embedded in the box rim, oriented so the magnets attract and hold the lid closed under normal handling. A separate small 'key' disc (30mm diameter, 6mm thick) has its own embedded 8mm magnet; when the key disc is pressed flat against a marked circular target printed on the top of the lid directly above the lid's magnet, the key's opposing magnetic pole repels/neutralizes the latch magnet's hold enough for the user to lift the lid open with light thumb pressure on a lid-edge finger notch. Purpose: A spoiler-proof, ceremonial storage box for tabletop legacy/campaign board games (such as Gloomhaven, Frosthaven, or Pandemic Legacy style games) that include sealed envelopes or boxes meant to be opened only at specific campaign milestones, used by a play group to store not-yet-opened content safely between sessions. Style: Understated and slightly mysterious, subtle beveled edges, a small embossed padlock or seal icon on the lid target zone, single solid dark color (customer-selectable) with no bright branding. Technical specification: External box dimensions approximately 100mm x 140mm x 55mm; internal compartment 90mm x 130mm x 40mm deep. Side card slot: 3mm wide x 90mm long, sized for one printed index card. 3 total printed parts (box, lid, key disc), single color PLA, 2 embedded 8mm x 3mm neodymium disc magnets in the lid/rim latch plus 1 in the key disc (3 magnets total), magnet pockets sized 8.2mm diameter x 3.1mm deep for a snug glue-free friction fit, lid-edge finger notch 15mm wide x 5mm deep for lifting.

ideas.title: Player-Aid Rail Clip
ideas.concept: A small C-shaped clip bracket with a vertical card slot that clamps onto the edge of a game box lid, table edge, or shelf up to 20mm thick, holding a single upright player-aid or reference card at eye level via a flexible printed snap-clamp arm.
ideas.rationale: Verifiable ongoing hobbyist behavior: multiple modern euro-style games ship with or are commonly supplemented by printed player-aid/reference cards (summary of icons, turn structure, scoring), and community-made card holder/rack accessories for board games appear repeatedly across Printables/Thingiverse/Etsy listings, indicating sustained buyer interest in keeping reference material visible at the table without occupying playing surface.
ideas.differentiation: Search found poker-style angled multi-card hand racks designed to fan a held hand of playing cards for card games. This product targets a different use case and geometry: a single-card vertical clamp-on display for a reference/player-aid card, mounted to a fixed surface edge rather than resting on the table in front of a player. Claim is scoped to that single-card, edge-clamping use case, not to card holders broadly.
ideas.producibility_notes: 1 part, single color PLA, one printed flex-snap clamp arm (a single flexible joint, low risk per the repeated-joint caution since there is only one). Critical dimension: card slot width 0.8mm +/- 0.1mm to hold a sleeved or unsleeved reference card snugly without excessive play.
ideas.margin_case: About 15g PLA, ~40 minutes print. Sell as a 4-pack for $30 ($7.50 each); low material cost but solves a specific recurring table-space annoyance for regular euro-game players, comparable in price to small acrylic card stands sold individually on Etsy.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a single C-shaped clamp bracket with a flexible printed snap-arm that clips onto a flat edge (game box lid, table edge, or shelf) between 0mm and 20mm thick, and a vertical slot on the front face of the bracket sized to hold one playing-card-size reference or player-aid card standing upright. Purpose: A table accessory for board-game players who use printed player-aid or reference cards during play and want them displayed upright and visible at eye level without occupying table space or requiring the player to hold the card. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, compact, single solid color (customer-selectable), no ornamentation, smooth edges for safe handling near a table edge. Technical specification: Overall bracket footprint approximately 40mm wide x 60mm tall x 25mm deep. The clamp opening is a flexible printed snap-arm (single living-hinge-style flex joint, not a repeated mechanism) that can flex to grip surfaces from 0mm to 20mm thick with consistent spring-back pressure; the card slot is 0.8mm wide (+/- 0.1mm tolerance) x 65mm wide x 15mm deep, angled 10 degrees back from vertical for stability. Single-part print, single color PLA, no assembly, no hardware, printable without supports when oriented with the clamp opening facing sideways.

ideas.title: Board Game Library Circulation Audit Tray
ideas.concept: A slim insert tray with a grid of generic labeled compartments in two size classes, plus a card-holder clip for a swappable printed checklist card, designed to sit inside a circulating library or game-cafe board game box so staff can visually confirm all small pieces are present at checkout and return.
ideas.rationale: Documented, verifiable institutional trend: public library 'Library of Things' programs with circulating board game collections are widely documented (Programming Librarian's 'Circulating Board Game Collection' guide, multiple public library websites, and WSU's dedicated Game Checkout Program libguide), and these programs report meaningful usage volumes (Hillsboro Public Library reports over 600 circulating board games), representing a real institutional buyer distinct from individual hobbyists.
ideas.differentiation: Search shows hobbyist organizer inserts on Printables/MakerWorld/Cults3D are consistently designed to fit one specific game's exact component list for permanent home storage. No result targeted the institutional circulation use case: a generic, relabelable audit tray with a swappable paper checklist meant to fit inside many different box sizes for quick piece-count verification rather than optimal packing. Claim is scoped to that specific institutional-audit framing, not to organizers generally.
ideas.producibility_notes: 2 parts (tray with 6-8 generic compartments in 2 size classes, plus a small card-holder clip for the checklist insert), single color PLA, offered in 3 standard footprint sizes (small/medium/large box) to cover common game box interiors without needing a fully custom part per title. No hardware, no assembly beyond snapping the card clip onto the tray edge.
ideas.margin_case: About 180g PLA, ~6hr print. Sell at $32 per unit for small institutional batch orders (libraries/game cafes typically order multiples for their circulating collection); justified against staff labor cost of manually recounting every component on each of hundreds of annual checkouts/returns.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a slim rectangular insert tray with a grid of 6-8 open compartments in two size classes (4 small compartments approximately 30mm x 30mm for tokens/meeples, 2-4 larger compartments approximately 60mm x 40mm for cards or larger pieces), plus a small clip on one long edge of the tray that holds a printed paper checklist card face-up. Purpose: An institutional inventory-audit tool for public libraries and board-game cafes that circulate board games for checkout, letting staff quickly visually scan the tray's compartments against a printed component checklist to confirm no pieces are missing before lending or after a game is returned, rather than being a permanent optimized storage solution for one specific game title. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, plain and durable, single solid neutral color (e.g. gray or black), no decorative elements, designed to look institutional rather than hobbyist. Technical specification: Provide 3 standard tray footprint sizes: Small (200mm x 200mm x 25mm deep), Medium (240mm x 240mm x 30mm deep), Large (280mm x 280mm x 35mm deep), each with the same relative compartment grid layout (4 small 30mm x 30mm bins, 3 larger 60mm x 40mm bins) scaled proportionally, plus a checklist card clip (a flat spring-clip slot 2mm wide x 90mm long) molded into one long edge sized for a standard index card. 2 parts per tray (tray body plus card clip, or card clip printed integrated as part of the tray if the flex geometry allows), single color PLA, no glue or hardware, no supports needed when printed with the compartment openings facing up.

ideas.title: Con Badge Charm Clips
ideas.concept: A set of 4 small rigid 3D printed charms (a d20 die, a meeple figure, a stack-of-three-meeples, and a dice-tower silhouette), each about 25mm tall with a 4mm-diameter ribbon hole at the top and an optional flat back panel that can be engraved with the attendee's name or a personal note, designed to clip onto a convention badge lanyard or ribbon chain.
ideas.rationale: Documented, active convention subculture: badge-ribbon trading and stacking ('badge beard' collecting) is described as an established practice at fan/tabletop conventions per CONvergence's own 'Ribbons' program page and multiple Etsy 'Con Badge Ribbon' listings, with tabletop-focused conventions like Gen Con drawing large attendee bases that actively collect and trade badge-attached novelties.
ideas.differentiation: Search confirms existing badge ribbons at conventions are fabric or printed-paper strips (pc/nametag adhesive ribbons, Etsy fabric ribbon listings), not rigid 3D printed charms. This product is a distinct physical form factor (a durable printed dice/meeple charm with a ribbon hole) rather than a ribbon, aimed at the same trading/stacking culture but as a keepsake object rather than a consumable paper strip. Claim is scoped to that specific format distinction, not to convention memorabilia broadly.
ideas.producibility_notes: 4 distinct single-part charm designs, single color PLA per charm (customer may order a themed 4-pack in one color or mixed colors), no assembly. Critical dimension: ribbon hole bore diameter 4mm clear (sized for a standard lanyard ribbon or a small carabiner clip) with 0.2mm print tolerance so the hole prints clean without needing post-processing drilling.
ideas.margin_case: About 8g PLA per charm, ~20 minutes print each. Sell as a 4-pack for $14; low material cost but priced as an impulse convention purchase/keepsake, comparable to the $3-6 per-item pricing seen on Etsy con-ribbon listings while offering a more durable, collectible object.
ideas.prompt: Concept: Design a set of 4 distinct small charm shapes: (1) a d20 icosahedron die with one flattened face showing a printed '20', (2) a simple meeple figure (rounded head, flared body) in profile relief, (3) a stack of three overlapping meeple silhouettes, and (4) a dice-tower silhouette (a simple tapering tower shape with a triangular roof). Each charm is a flat-relief pendant with a small hole at the top for threading onto a ribbon or lanyard, and a flat back panel suitable for an optional debossed name or short text (up to 12 characters). Purpose: A convention keepsake/trading item for tabletop board-game convention attendees (such as Gen Con or similar events) who participate in badge-ribbon collecting and trading culture, worn clipped to a badge lanyard or ribbon chain. Style: Bold, simple, high-contrast silhouette shapes readable at a glance from a few feet away (as trading items are seen across a room), single solid color per charm (customer-selectable per charm or per set), smooth edges safe for pocket carry. Technical specification: Each charm is approximately 25mm tall x 20mm wide x 4mm thick. Ribbon hole: 4mm diameter, centered 3mm from the top edge, with 1.5mm of surrounding material for strength. Optional back-panel text: debossed 0.4mm deep, minimum stroke width 1mm, auto-scaled to fit up to 12 characters within a 16mm x 8mm text zone. 4 total single-part printed charms per set, single color PLA per charm, no assembly, no hardware beyond the customer's own ribbon/lanyard, no supports required when printed flat-face-down.
